newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek bonds rally on lower rates, stronger drachma.
newsitem.headline: Greek bonds rally on lower rates, stronger drachma.

text.p: Yields on Greek fixed coupon bonds fell a tenth of a point across-the-board in active mid-session dealings on sharply lower depo rates and a stronger drachma, dealers said.

"Yields on fixed-rate bonds have dropped 10 basis points across-the-board at mid-session," a senior bond dealer at a private bank said. "Lower interbank rates and the strengthening of the drachma against the ecu are the driving forces behind the rally."
Gross yields on three-, five-and seven-year bonds have fallen to 9.48 percent, 9.07 percent and 8.83 percent respectively, the dealer said.
"We see no offers for floating rate notes," he said. "There are just bids right now which shows that market sentiment has improved dramatically."
The central bank intervened and sold an unspecified amount of $ for drachmas pushing ecu/drachma below 311 earlier on.

"The central bank wants to burn those speculators who moved against the drachma in recent days," said Panos Panayiotopoulos, assistant treasurer at private Alpha Bank. "Drachma is sharply up against the ecu trading around 310.30/50."
Ecu/drachma opened at 312 but fell sharply to 311.40/50 on ecu selling from domestic players before the central bank intervened and pushed it to 310.20/50.

"The central bank did the right thing," he said. "It supported the drachma, sold a small portion of its forex reserves at high levels reducing surplus interbank liquidity and is now going to punish speculators by forcing them to pay the points and take the forex loss."
Bank of Greece sold more than 1.2 billion ecus this week to shore up the drachma.

Depo rates were off early morning peaks, trading 100 to 150 basis points lower to 11 percent from one-month to three-month tenors and 50 to 70 basis points to 10.40 percent in six-month to one-year periods, dealers said.
"The market was very nervous and volatile this morning but it has turned around around mid-session," a money dealer said. "It is a much calmer market right now."
Forex forwards were also trading lower around mid-session with the drop more accentuated in the long-end of the curve. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
